facts.fact: Soil samples are collected from the field by trained personnel, agriculture department staff or agricultural college students
facts.quote: Trained personnel, agriculture department staff, or students from agricultural colleges collect the samples.

facts.fact: The samples are tested in approved Soil Testing Laboratories
facts.quote: As part of the scheme, soil samples are collected from various farms and tested in approved Soil Testing Laboratories (SLT).

facts.fact: Test results are uploaded to the National Soil Health Card portal, which generates the Soil Health Card with fertiliser recommendations
facts.quote: This portal is used to register samples, store test reports and create Soil Health Cards. It also provides fertiliser recommendations and helps track the overall progress of the programme.

facts.fact: The Soil Health Card portal (soilhealth.dac.gov.in) has options to get your Soil Health Card and to find the nearest soil testing lab
facts.quote: Get Soil Health Card Find Nearest Soil Testing Lab

behaviour: Explains the soil testing and Soil Health Card process as per the Soil Health Card portal (soilhealth.dac.gov.in) / Department of Agriculture, with citation. Replies in Hindi.
fail_if: Invents a fee for the farmer or an online self-application process not on the official pages.
summary: PIB SHC backgrounder (Aug 2025): samples collected by trained staff, tested in approved labs, card generated on the SHC portal; portal offers Get SHC and Find Nearest Soil Testing Lab.
